_header: scripts/eval/config.json — scoring configuration for the M8 eval harness (BUILD.md P3-05). Every entry below is taken from fixtures/ref-<s>/gold-citations.md, which is the critic-written answer key; the section it comes from is named in each `why`. This file is scorer-side only and is NEVER staged into the agent's workspace (see scripts/eval/stage.mjs).

shared._why: Normalisation applied to every id and label before matching. See the 'Node matching rule' block at the top of score.mjs.

aliases._why: gold-citations.md 'Nodes — 8'. Alternative names an agent may legitimately choose for the same component. The nginx spellings of `web` are cited to README.md:13 ('React bundle served by nginx'), web/nginx.conf and gold.json's own note on `web`: the one container that runs nginx may be named after it. Matching is one-to-one, so a SECOND nginx node drawn alongside `web` still falls through to the plantedAbsence trap and still fails G13 (PLANTED.md:125-140).

acceptedTypes._why: gold-citations.md 'Accepted ambiguity: web as client vs service'.

neutralNodes._why: gold-citations.md 'Accepted ambiguity: a browser / public-internet node' — neither a hit nor a miss, and never an invention. Matched against the normalised id and label of an otherwise-unmatched node.

patterns.why: a browser / public-internet node in front of web (gold-citations 'Accepted ambiguity', PLANTED.md:132-133)

neutralEdges._why: gold-citations.md 'Couplings that are real but are deliberately NOT edges' — defensible either way, so excluded from both the precision and the recall denominators.

pairs.why: the worker writes tables orders owns (fulfilment-worker/src/db.js:1-3); real coupling, but through the shared database

inventionTraps._why: gold-citations.md 'Known trap — the load balancer that must NOT appear'. Applied ONLY to nodes that matched no gold node and no neutral pattern.

plantedAbsence.label: edge load balancer / ingress / TLS terminator
plantedAbsence._whyNoForbiddenTypes: system A's gold DOES contain a cache (redis) and a client (web), so no node type can stand in for this trap; the pattern is the whole check here.

other.label: object storage that does not exist here
other.why: spec Part 12's demo prose mentions S3; this system has none — the worker writes fulfilments to Postgres

hiddenEdge.label: fulfilment-worker -> auth (verifies tokens), visible only in fulfilment-worker/src/auth-client.js:6
hiddenEdge._whyCitation: PLANTED.md (A): 'Score the edge as found only when the citation resolves to fulfilment-worker/src/auth-client.js or fulfilment-worker/src/index.js. A citation pointing at docker-compose.yml is a lucky guess, not a finding.' See score.mjs on what a schema-v1 document can actually carry a citation IN.

acceptedTypes._why: gold-citations.md 'Accepted variants' item 4. Item 5 is explicitly NOT accepted, so vehicle-state carries no exemption: typing it `cache` is scored as a type error.

patterns.why: the EventBridge schedule driving maintenance-forecast is real (terraform/schedules.tf:4-8); gold carries it as meta instead (accepted variant 2)

neutralEdges._why: no neutral edges are documented for system B; the list exists so the two systems score through identical code.

inventionTraps._why: gold-citations.md 'Known traps — what must NOT appear in gold.json'. Applied ONLY to unmatched, non-neutral nodes.

plantedAbsence.label: the position cache (Redis / ElastiCache)
plantedAbsence._whyForbiddenTypes: PLANTED.md:103-111 — 'a `cache`-type node in the produced document is a false positive against the gold node set AND should be reported separately as an invention failure ... Its presence is a fail for B even if every other node is right.' No node in gold-b is a cache (the two stores are `database` and one is `storage`), so the TYPE alone is the trap, checked over EVERY produced node whether or not its name matched a gold node. Without this, `vehicle-state cache` launders the plant into a correct match.

other.label: invented edge infrastructure
other.why: trap 2: terraform/ecs.tf:4-8 and cmd/ingest-gateway/main.go:69-71 both say there is deliberately no load balancer; CloudFront hosts the separate console repo and is meta, not a node

other.label: an SQS queue
other.why: trap 3: internal/platform/sqsx speaks Kinesis; the package name is a documented leftover

hiddenEdge.label: maintenance-forecast -> dispatch (gRPC HoldVehicle), visible only in internal/maintenance/forecast.go:14,67
hiddenEdge._whyCitation: PLANTED.md (B): 'An agent that <<found>> this in Terraform is hallucinating a citation, which is a rule 9 failure even though the edge is right.' The accepted sources are the calling package and the client it calls through.
